notes:
Summary: enterprise procurement focused on Dedicated capacity + strict SLA. Primary workload: real-time trading risk scoring (low jitter, high availability), secondary: embeddings and reranking for risk signal enrichment. Cost sensitivity: mid-high; willing to commit to 12+ reserved GPUs for guaranteed throughput if SLA acceptable.

Key SLA asks from Strandbridge (negotiation points):
- Uptime target: legal prefers 99.99% monthly for production endpoints; engineering will accept 99.95% if credits meaningful.
- Credit schedule: propose sliding credits: 10% monthly credit for <99.95%, 25% for <99.9%, 50% for <99.0% (we proposed a custom schedule to Legal). Redwood initial counter: 5% / 20% / 40% respectively. Legal to meet on 3/24.
- Maintenance windows: Strandbridge requires max 4 hours/month planned maintenance on production clusters; maintenance must be scheduled with 72h notice and allowed outside US market hours (primary market 08:00-18:00 ET). Redwood prefers scheduled 6 hours/month.
- Emergency maintenance: only with on-call approval; must provide mitigation plan and ability to failover to secondary region or model variant.
- Support SLAs: P1 acknowledge <= 15 minutes, P1 workaround <= 1 hour, P2 acknowledge <= 1 hour, P2 workaround <= 4 hours. Redwood's standard: P1 30m ack / 4h workaround — major gap. SE to push for enterprise tier.
- Throughput guarantees: committed capacity to support 500 concurrent chat sessions with 150 token/sec average per session without >5% tail latency penalty. Reserved GPU planning: Strandbridge intends to reserve 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (initial), with burst allocation up to +20% for market spikes. Need explicit routing/fallback policy for bursts.
- Data residency & audit: all inference logs kept in VPC for 90 days, audit logs exported to Strandbridge SIEM, KMS control required. Redlines in security doc (drive link).
